name: Soroush Shahbaznejad
bio: I am a Ph.D. student in Color Science at the Munsell Color Science Laboratory, Rochester Institute of Technology, advised by Prof. Mekides Assefa Abebe. My research lies at the intersection of human visual perception, material appearance, and computer vision.

I investigate how people perceive glossiness, texture, and translucency, and whether pretrained vision foundation models capture these perceptual attributes. My work combines psychophysical experiments, computational color science, and deep learning to study the relationship between visual representations and human perception.
My long-term interests include perceptually informed representation learning, material appearance modeling, and controllable image generation.
themes: Measuring human judgments of glossiness, texture, and translucency through psychophysical experiments and perceptual rating analysis, and relating perceived appearance to material properties.
Evaluating frozen pretrained models, including DINOv2, CLIP, MAE, and iBOT, against human perceptual judgments using linear and kernel probing and representational similarity analysis.
Studying color spaces and color-based data augmentation for material and skin segmentation, alongside color appearance modeling and image representation analysis.
Contributing to collaborative psychophysical studies of emissive color appearance, reference-white placement, and highlight tone mapping for HDR image reproduction.
